content:
Google launched its brand-new Pixel 11 series at the beginning of the month. Although the phone doesn't differ much from the previous-generation Pixel 10, it adds several thoughtful user experience improvements. One of them is a new camera processing option that gives you more granular control over how your photos turn out.

With the iPhone 18 Pro on the horizon, I'm hoping Apple will add a similar feature.

The Pixel 11 introduces a new camera feature called 'Camera Looks'. To some extent, this feature is similar to 'Photographic Styles' on the iPhone, allowing users to adjust the way their phone takes photos. This kind of adjustment is made before shooting and is more than just a simple filter.

Google offers several preset style options similar to Apple's, and you can fine-tune the effect for each preset. Beyond that, there are several new options that capture emerging photography trends, including Editorial, Velvet, Classic, Digi, Black Tie, and Minimal.

These Looks are deliberately designed to move away from the over-processed feel of smartphone photos, attempting to recapture the flavour of old-school photography. True to its name, Digi aims to recreate the low dynamic range, high contrast, and grainy look of those small, pocket-sized cameras from the 2010s.

As for Minimal, it takes a completely low-processing approach. Most HDR processing is disabled, so essentially you'll see what the smartphone image sensor actually captures. You can check out some sample photos over at 9to5Google.

In theory, using the ProRAW format on the iPhone, you can roll back an iPhone photo to what appears to be a relatively unprocessed state, but doing so somewhat defeats the purpose of shooting with a phone.

Summary

If Apple wants to build the best pocket camera on the market, it needs to understand that not every user wants the same thing. 'Photographic Styles' is a good start, but Apple can go further. After all, photography is an art of self-expression, so giving users more options to control the degree of photo processing will be a very important step. Apple should take a page out of Google's book and add a 'Minimal' style to the iPhone as well.

What do you think of the iPhone's current photography performance? Do you like Apple's latest 'Photographic Styles'? Or do you feel it still falls short? I'd love to hear your thoughts—please share them in the comments section.
